title: Ingress Readiness — Scenario Sizing & Headroom (Q3 2026)
content:
Purpose:
This sheet is an operationally-focused sizing and headroom plan for the public ingress plane (hosted API) for the Q3-2026 planning horizon. Goal: produce simple, actionable targets (tokens/sec and QPS) by region and workload profile, map to GPU pool slices, and recommend short-term changes for autoscaling/prewarming and fallback policies.

Executive summary (short):
- We model three workload profiles: chat-low-latency (A), bulk-embeddings (B), and burst-rerank/search (C).
- Baseline projected 90th percentile QPS/tokens for global peak week (worst-of-region) is estimated at ~1.9M QPS-equivalent requests and ~95M tokens/sec across workloads combined for Q3 end-of-quarter spike scenario.
- Recommended steady-state headroom: 30% regional buffer for high-variability regions (us-west-2, ap-southeast-1), 20% for eu-west-1.
- Recommend immediate provisioning: reserve an additional 3 H100 slices in us-west-2 and convert 20% of cold A100 capacity to prewarmed H100-backed pools for chat-low-latency.

Assumptions used in projections:
- Profile A (chat-low-latency): avg request 40 tokens, latency target <200ms p95, high concurrency.
- Profile B (embeddings): avg request 1024 tokens, batch-friendly, throughput prioritized over latency.
- Profile C (rerank/search): avg request 150 tokens, short bursts, sensitive to tail latency.
- Model mix: mix of LLaMA-2-70B (quantized), FLAN variants, and a small % of larger open models; projection converts model mix to tokens/sec via per-token GPU throughput matrix (see bottom).
- Growth: baseline organic growth of 18% month-over-month for strategic customers + 1–3 large-burst customers (onboarding risk).

Regional projection snapshot (peak week, worst-hour) — simplified table: 
| Region | Profile A QPS | Profile A tokens/s | Profile B QPS | Profile B tokens/s | Profile C QPS | Profile C tokens/s | Total tokens/s | Notes |
| us-west-2 | 42k | 1.68M | 6k | 6.14M | 28k | 4.2M | 12.02M | high-variance (mobile apps) |
| eu-west-1 | 30k | 1.2M | 4.5k | 4.6M | 18k | 2.7M | 8.5M | steady enterprise traffic |
| ap-southeast-1 | 26k | 1.04M | 3k | 3.07M | 22k | 3.3M | 7.41M | peak-hour bursts, lower cold-warm ratio |
| other (aggregate) | 12k | 0.48M | 2k | 2.05M | 10k | 1.5M | 4.03M | smaller markets aggregate |
Total (global) tokens/sec ~= 31.96M (per-hour peak slice) — note: this is conservative for a single peak hour; projecting up to 3 concurrent peak hours across timezones results in worst-case ~95M tokens/sec sustained across GPUs.

GPU mapping & suggested pool slices:
- Chat-low-latency (Profile A): prioritize H100 for critical routes. Target pool slices: 60% H100 (prewarmed), 30% A100-80 for warmed but lower concurrency, 10% L40s for cheap inference variants.
- Embeddings (Profile B): batch-friendly on A100 and L40s. Target pool slices: 70% A100 (batched), 30% L40s quantized.
- Rerank/Search (Profile C): H100 + A100 mix for tail performance. Target pool slices: 50% H100, 45% A100, 5% L40s.

Headroom targets (operational):
- Region-level soft-headroom (recommended): us-west-2: 30% (because of mobile traffic spikes); eu-west-1: 20%; ap-southeast-1: 30%; other: 25%.
- Pool-level safety slices: maintain 2 warm H100 nodes per critical pool as prewarm standby; maintain 10% of A100 pool as warm spare for embeddings.
- Token/sec safety stock: maintain ability to absorb a 50% sudden surge on Profile C for up to 10 minutes via burst routing to dedicated reserved capacity and fallbacks.

Autoscaling / prewarm rules (short checklist):
- Prewarm trigger: projected moving-average tokens/sec for next 15 minutes > 80% of pool capacity for 3 consecutive minutes -> prewarm one H100 node.
- Warm tier timeouts: keep prewarmed nodes idle up to 12 minutes before scale-down during peak windows (09:00–02:00 UTC).
- Rapid fallback: if a pool falls below 70% available tokens/sec capacity for p95 latency SLA, route new requests to cheaper-but-slower quantized variant with per-request telemetry tag.

Operational playbook snippets (for on-call/SRE):
- If observed tokens/sec exceeds projected by >20% for 5+ minutes: 1) trigger burst-reserve plan; 2) notify capacity-on-call; 3) activate cross-region spillover rules (eu->us-west, ap->us-west) with degraded SLA flag.
- For model-serving failures (kernels OOM or slow kernels): fallback to nearest compatible quantized variant and mark routing policy to avoid the failing node for 30 minutes.

Short cost/impact notes:
- Converting 20% of cold A100 capacity to prewarm H100 carries a near-term cost delta (~+12% hourly spend for those nodes) but reduces p95 tail latency violations risk by estimated 40% for Profile A.
- Embeddings batching strategy expected to reduce effective tokens/sec GPU spend by ~22% if we increase max-batch-window from 10ms to 40ms for non-latency-critical customers.

Action items (next 30 days):
- [Owner: Maya] Run a synthetic replay for the top-10 customers into the simulated SLO model to validate the 95M tokens/sec worst-case assumption (Jira INFRA-1423).
- [Owner: Ravi] Prepare 3 H100 on-demand slices in us-west-2 and test prewarm + scale-down cycle under load.
- [Owner: Noah] Add telemetry tags for per-request model-variant routing to detect fallback rates; create a dashboard.
- [Owner: Eng-SRE] Document cross-region spillover play in Confluence and run a war-room drill.

Open questions / risks:
- How many large customers will adopt dedicated capacity in Q3 (reduces hosted demand but may create sudden ingress drop patterns)? Unknown — flagged for commercial.
- Model mix drift: if high-quality LLM adoption increases, tokens-per-request may increase; we need weekly model-mix telemetry to re-evaluate.

Appendix: throughput matrix (simple numbers used in calc)
- H100 (fp16, chat mix): ~24k tokens/sec per GPU (low-latency config).
- A100-80 (quantized / batched embeddings): ~12k tokens/sec per GPU at 1k-token batch sizes.
- L40s (quantized small): ~6k tokens/sec per GPU.

Notes / references:
- See linked artifacts (Jira & PR) for the replay harness and load-generator configs.
- Slack thread: #infra-capacity referenced on 2026-05-12 (thread id: C02Q9J3KL).

Comments (notes-to-self style):
- This is intentionally conservative on tokens/sec; I'd rather overprovision a small amount now and tighten once the replay confirms model mix.
- Need product input on acceptable degraded-mode SLA for cross-region spillovers (currently assumed -20% throughput target).
